summary_html: Agency **files a court petition** to open a **dependency** (or similar) case. Federal funding frameworks (IV-E/ASFA) link court oversight, reasonable-efforts findings, and permanency timelines to downstream actions.
authority_html:
- **ASFA / SSA Title IV-E** — court findings; timelines; permanency planning  
- **CFSR (45 CFR Part 1355)** — federal review of court/agency performance measures

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.holding: The court affirmed adjudications of dependency and findings of aggravated circumstances, holding that clear and convincing evidence of a sibling's severe abuse and of the mother's knowledge supported adjudicating both children dependent.
key_cases.relevance: Confirms that a dependency petition may reach a non-injured sibling on proof of abuse to the other child.
key_cases.quote: the trial court was correct in adjudicating L.P. dependent because there was clear and convincing evidence that R.P. was the victim of abuse

key_cases.holding: The court reversed the Superior Court, holding that a child whose non-custodial parent is ready, willing and able to provide proper care does not meet the Juvenile Act definition of a dependent child and may not be adjudicated dependent.
key_cases.relevance: Sets the threshold the agency must clear before a dependency petition can succeed.
key_cases.quote: a child is not dependent if the child has a parent who is willing and able to provide proper care to the child

key_cases.holding: The court affirmed the dependency adjudication of a child certified as a near fatality, holding the trial court did not abuse its discretion where medical evidence established extensive inflicted injuries and the mother failed to seek treatment.
key_cases.relevance: States the clear-and-convincing standard the agency must meet on its dependency petition.
key_cases.quote: In order to adjudicate a child dependent, the court must determine that the above definition has been met by clear and convincing evidence.

key_cases.case_name: Ernst v. Child & Youth Services of Chester County
key_cases.court: United States Court of Appeals for the Third Circuit
key_cases.holding: The court affirmed judgment for the agency defendants on absolute-immunity grounds, holding that child-welfare workers act in a quasi-prosecutorial capacity when they prepare for, initiate and prosecute dependency proceedings and are absolutely immune from § 1983 damages for those acts.
key_cases.relevance: Filing and prosecuting the dependency petition is a quasi-prosecutorial function, immunized from damages suits.
key_cases.quote: we hold that the CYS defendants are entitled to absolute immunity for their actions on behalf of the state in preparing for, initiating, and prosecuting dependency proceedings

key_cases.holding: Affirming the Superior Court, the court held that a court-ordered change of the permanency goal is not a condition precedent to an agency's filing of a petition to terminate parental rights, consistent with ASFA's endorsement of concurrent planning.
key_cases.relevance: Establishes the sequencing between dependency permanency review and the filing of a termination petition.
key_cases.quote: We conclude that Section 6351 does not require that a goal change precede the filing of a termination petition.

state_agency.name: Pennsylvania Department of Human Services, Office of Children, Youth, and Families

timeline_requirements.deadline: 60 days in all cases; reasons for delay must be recorded if not completed within 30 days
timeline_requirements.starts_from: Investigation commenced by the county agency
timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: The particular reasons for delay past 30 days must be described in the child protective service record and made available to the department to determine whether the county agency strictly followed 23 Pa.C.S. Ch. 63 and whether it is subject to action under 23 Pa.C.S. § 6343

timeline_requirements.deadline: 90 days to request an administrative review by, or appeal and request a hearing before, the secretary to amend or expunge an indicated report; the department sends notice of the secretary's decision within 60 days of a request for administrative review
timeline_requirements.starts_from: Notice to a person named as perpetrator, or to a school employee named, of the status of the indicated report
